title: BY HOW MUCH DO BATTERIES CUT CURTAILMENT
subtitle: Days with more charging see more curtailment, even with solar and the month held fixed

chart.x_label: battery charging, GWh in the day

callouts.label: Curtailment on low and high charging days, MWh a day

why: Over 405 days from 2025-08-24 to 2026-10-06, CAISO curtailed 13,827 MWh a day on average while its batteries charged 48,649 MWh a day. On the days with charging at or below the median (50,752 MWh), curtailment averaged 8,281 MWh; above it, 19,401. Charging alone goes with 699 MWh of curtailment per GWh charged; with solar output held fixed, 951; with the month too, 1,081 (standard error 172, p 0.000, R2 0.65). Solar output itself goes with -284 MWh of curtailment per GWh (standard error 54). The raw association and the controlled one can differ in sign: sunny spring days bring both charging and curtailment, so the question is what charging adds on a day like any other, and that is the third estimate. What it cannot separate is the batteries' dispatch from the prices that call for it.
footnote: Data: caiso_curtailment_daily (CAISO production and curtailment report, MWh a day; 'solar and wind' is curtailed_solar_mwh plus curtailed_wind_mwh, 'solar only' the first), caiso_battery_storage (Today's Outlook, batteries MW every 5 minutes; charging is the negative values summed times 5/60, a day needs at least 276 of its 288 intervals), caiso_fuel_supply (Today's Outlook, solar MW by hour summed to MWh, at least 23 hours), all on America/Los_Angeles days, 2025-08-24 to 2026-10-06, 405 days in 15 calendar months (the battery series begins 2025-08-24). Regressions: OLS of daily curtailment (MWh) on charging (GWh); on charging and solar (GWh); on both and month-of-sample dummies; HC1 standard errors (Stata's vce(robust)), p from Student's t. The split at the median charging day is a plain comparison of means. No instrument, no event window: an association.

rows.measure: charging, solar output and month held fixed

effect_table.in_words: each extra GWh a day of charging goes with 1,081 MWh more curtailment, solar output and the month held fixed (standard error 172, p 0.000): the batteries charge on the days the grid has most to spare

source_line: Source: CAISO production and curtailment report; CAISO Today's Outlook (storage, fuel source); ERW tables caiso_curtailment_daily, caiso_battery_storage, caiso_fuel_supply.
